body: DIRECT-INPUT IDENTITY COURT, found by reading the existing core test rather than inferring the API. AtlasSuite lines 22-27 deliberately prove that Hello-world inputs with different line endings and blank runs have the same StoryId and canonicalChecksum but different rawChecksum; StorySource.fromText derives the default StoryId from canonical content. Therefore StoryId alone is not a lawful CLI invocation, cache, publication-directory, or bundle identity. The direct-input slice must bind at least original byte checksum plus charset/BOM/decoder disposition, decoded raw checksum, canonical checksum, and canonicalization policy. Add a court with two byte-distinct files that canonicalize identically: they may share semantic StoryId and SurfaceAtlas coordinates, but they must retain distinct intake receipts and must not overwrite, cache-hit, or replay one another as the same invocation. A mutant that keys output only by StoryId or canonicalChecksum must fail. This is the main condition under which direct text input is sound rather than a lossy convenience path.
